results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 55 paragraph summaries match the controlling ideas of p01-p55 in spec order (Architecture now after Experimenting on Ranking and Prices); the five callouts match no spec paragraph, as expected.

results.quote: Who decides: the Head of Data & ML owns the engine, the methods and the cluster maps;
results.finding: The reverse outliner needed two summaries (decision ownership / metrics to watch). The paragraph has two labelled parts, 'Who decides:' and 'What to watch:', and the spec's p52 controlling idea itself joins the two (ownership split ... and the estimate-to-rollout gap as report card). Fix by splitting p52 into two units or recasting it around one idea in the spec.
Every unit aligns to a spec paragraph that supports S1-S5 or is an intro/scene/transition unit of its section; no orphan paragraphs.

Tables and figures have lead-ins or follow-up sentences saying what they show (bump table -> p07 arithmetic; retest table -> p46; design table 'coarser units mean less interference and less power'; Holtz quotation glossed and tied to the bump test).

Each declared boundary is expressed: e.g. 'Once the design fixes the unit' (metrics), 'Every design, metric and review above needs platform support' (architecture, cause_effect), 'The bump test is one case of interference' (elaboration), 'Ignore these defaults' (failure modes, contrast). p03's opening picks up interference only mid-paragraph ('changes that only looked like wins'); judged acceptable.

Every does_not_know term is defined at or before first use (SUTVA p01, interference p02, Concepts table for units/cluster/guardrail, primary metric and exposure p12, two-sided p23, carryover p31, synthetic control p32, interleaving p33, holdout glossed p36, SRM/CUPED/sequential in the p17 table). Both flow readers flagged Hearthly, Motorvane and Valuo as unglossed (A7, A11, B12), but audience.already_knows lists Veldmark's brands and Valuo, so they are known to the declared audience; a cheap gloss is still worth adding. Single-reader items (72-hour fraud restatement A9, Adevinta's 2025 decentralization A10, 'registered' before the registry B8) are not on does_not_know and are recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.quote: My reading of that path is the recommendation in this chapter's first key point

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: The Bump That Ate Itself ¶4
results.quote: bump purchases were up only 22% on the same weeks of the previous year, not 48% (1.22 × 1.99 ÷ 2.49 ≈ 0.975), so revenue ran roughly €950,000 a year below the old price instead of €6.8 million above it
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read the turn of the story: one sentence packs a new year-over-year baseline, an inline calculation and two euro figures. Split it so each comparison is its own sentence.

results.draft_locus: Metrics: Liquidity First, Revenue Second, Both Watched ¶4
results.quote: That is why results are computed as a stream while a test runs
results.finding: Both readers read 'That is why' as presupposing streaming computation that has not been introduced (it appears only in the Adevinta paragraph of Architecture). State it as a requirement ('so results must be computed as a stream while a test runs') rather than as an established fact.

results.quote: it was designed under the experimentation standard Veldmark adopted in June 2027, after the bump test, which this chapter sets out after the architecture.
results.finding: Both readers stumbled: the sentence jumps the timeline to autumn 2027, names a standard not yet shown, ends in a navigational aside, and 'which' can attach to the bump test or the standard. Split the sentence and make the referent unambiguous (or shorten the aside).

results.quote: Veldmark learned this the hard way: the September 2027 ranking-policy experiment in [[ranking]] and the bump-price retest in the next section could not share Tradeyard NL's clusters.
results.finding: Both readers stopped here: it is the first mention that a retest exists, buried in a bullet, and 'learned this the hard way' oversells a scheduling constraint that was avoided by moving the retest to Belgium. Drop the 'hard way' framing and introduce the retest plainly (reader A also read 'next section' as the next subsection).

results.quote: The €1.99 price had stayed live in the Netherlands until the retest's result was reviewed
results.finding: Both readers were surprised that a price known since June to lose money stayed live until December; arriving as a past-perfect aside in the last story paragraph, it reads as an inconsistency. The draft could announce at the post-mortem (p43) that the price stayed live pending a retest, but no reason exists in the ledger (decision log 2026-11-12 declined to invent one), so whether this is fixable in the prose alone or needs a scenario decision is for the author.

results.quote: Ignore these defaults and experimentation fails in recognizable ways.
results.finding: Reader B marked Vertical Differences' position unclear: 'these defaults' points back past the vertical table to the trade-off table. Reader A found the link clear. One reader only.

results.quote: This is called **interference**: the outcome of a unit depends on the treatment of other units.
results.finding: Reader B first read 'This' as naming the transfer, not the dependence that causes it. One reader only.

results.quote: The February bump test had neither, and the three cases below show what such a review must look for.
results.finding: Reader B had to map 'neither' back to owner and registration/review, and 'registered' assumes a registry introduced only in Architecture. One reader only.
